assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental markets and strategic-reasoning research made controlled experiments a central, policy-relevant method in economics and transformed evidence on behavior in strategic settings.
assessment.attribution: Plott, Holt, and Camerer represent foundational experimental-market design, institutional testing, and behavioural game-theory development; the intellectual lineage is broad but this trio is strongly identified with the contribution.
assessment.maturity: The methods and findings have accumulated over decades, shaped multiple fields, and remain actively used.
uncertainties: A three-person award cannot fully encompass other major experimental-economics contributors.
The contribution joins methodological and substantive advances that may be difficult to formulate as one citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis and measurement of reciprocity, fairness, and inequity aversion fundamentally changed economic models of incentives, cooperation, and institutions.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt are especially central to the canonical modelling and experimental evidence, while Falk is a major contributor to the empirical and behavioural programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has been extensively replicated, integrated into economic theory, and applied across labour, organisational, and public economics.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed across a large experimental and theoretical literature.
The empirical scope and stability of particular social-preference measures remain active research questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research on mobility supplied influential measurement, credible empirical designs, and direct evidence on the geography and determinants of opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are closely associated with the core mobility and opportunity-atlas research programme, though important antecedents and collaborators exist.
assessment.maturity: Its datasets, empirical approaches, and findings have changed research and public debate, with a substantial body of follow-on work.
uncertainties: The literature is comparatively recent relative to classic prize themes.
Causal interpretation of place-based mobility patterns and policy implications remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory and measurement of selection in insurance markets provided a durable framework for studying market failures and designing health and social insurance.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie jointly span the leading empirical and theoretical advances, though the subject rests on earlier foundational information economics.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established and has generated a deep empirical literature with clear policy relevance.
uncertainties: The proposed grouping covers several related rather than a single sharply bounded discovery.
Attribution relative to the older adverse-selection literature requires careful citation design.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made credible empirical analysis of persistent processes with unobserved heterogeneity feasible across much of applied economics.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are the clearest originators of the signature estimator; Blundell's subsequent system-GMM work is central to the mature contribution.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding, exceptionally influential, and continually scrutinized through a large applied and methodological literature.
uncertainties: Widespread misuse and weak-instrument problems complicate the practical legacy.
The award's broad methodological impact must be weighed against narrower public visibility.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence and audit studies made discrimination measurable through transparent field experiments and established an enduring empirical research design.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are strongly identified with the landmark modern correspondence-study contribution, while the broader audit-method tradition has many predecessors.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been widely extended across markets and countries and remains central to evidence on discrimination.
uncertainties: Field-experimental estimates isolate particular stages of market interaction rather than all channels of discrimination.
Credit for the general audit methodology extends well beyond the proposed laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification and moment-inequality methods gave economics principled tools for drawing credible conclusions when point identification is unavailable.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the central intellectual originator; Tamer and Molinari made major contributions to econometric development and application of the programme.
assessment.maturity: The framework is theoretically mature, broadly used in econometrics, and increasingly important for transparent treatment of weak assumptions.
uncertainties: Its impact is more methodological and less visible to the wider economics profession than some alternatives.
The field contains substantial additional contributors whose roles would need careful delimitation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of present bias, self-control, and reference dependence reshaped behavioural economics and influenced analysis of saving, consumption, and policy design.
assessment.attribution: Laibson and O'Donoghue are central to formal present-bias and self-control models, while Rabin made foundational contributions to behavioural economic theory.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are deeply embedded in modern behavioural economics and have generated extensive empirical and policy research.
uncertainties: The proposed citation combines distinct behavioural mechanisms with overlapping intellectual histories.
Empirical magnitudes and external validity of behavioural parameters remain heterogeneous across settings.
